description: We are Supernova Spark, two Panamanian sisters passionate about space. Our love for the stars grew by sharing it with each other, and we strongly believe in a generational relay to pass down knowledge, spark curiosity, and prove that science belongs to all of us. Together we created The Iron Siblings, an illustrated story about NASA’s Mars rovers and Voyager spacecraft. 🚀💗
summary: Spirit, Opportunity and the two Voyagers are still out there, far from home, and their stories deserve to be known. With The Iron Siblings, we turned them into characters in an illustrated book told by two sisters under the night sky. Our project answers the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge by combining real NASA images and mission data with storytelling, vivid illustrations and simple language for young readers. Our story is inspired by our own childhood, when our love for the stars grew by sharing it with each other. It is a bridge between science and imagination, made for families, classrooms and anyone who loves space.
details:
The Iron Siblings is an illustrated digital storybook told through two sisters who read, under the night sky, the story of the machines NASA left behind. Two chapters and an epilogue follow Spirit and Opportunity on Mars and Voyager 1 and 2 in deep space, as if they were siblings too. Five notes tucked into the pages reveal real NASA images, mission data and a hidden “Did you know?”. The sisters in the book represent us as children: the story is inspired by our own childhood, when our love for the stars grew by sharing it with each other. The concept, the story, the characters and the illustration ideas are ours; the tools helped us bring them to life.

How we built it

  • HTML5, CSS and JavaScript in a single file, with no install
  • CSS 3D page-turn effect (flipbook)
  • Web Audio API for soft synthesized sound and Web Speech API for optional narration
  • Responsive layout that adapts the text to laptop and phone screens
  • Google Fonts: Caveat, Lora, Cormorant Garamond
  • Creation tools: Google Gemini (AI, illustrations), Canva (design tool, not AI) and Claude (AI, code and text help)
  • Hosting: Netlify for the project and Google Drive for the demo PDF

 What makes it special

  • Narrative Design: two sisters frame the story, and the machines become siblings who pass the journey on, like a relay.
  • A Story Rooted in Real Life: the two sisters in the book represent us as children, and the story is inspired by our own childhood.
  • Educational Value: every NASA note offers a real image, its source and a “Did you know?” in simple language.
  • Data Trust: dates, places and facts checked against NASA mission pages, and each note links to its source.
  • Gentle Experience: sound and narration are optional and only start after a click, and no login is needed.
